newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Escondida union presents wage demands Tues.
newsitem.headline: Chile Escondida union presents wage demands Tues.

text.p: The only union at Chile's huge Escondida copper mine will present a labor deal to management Tuesday in the first collective wage talks at the pit, said union adviser Salvador Barrientos.
"This is the first collective negotiation at Escondida," Barrientos told Reuters by telephone from Antofagasta.
"Our main objective is to get Escondida to accept the fact of the union's existence."
The mining company has been hostile towards the union which was set up three years ago, said Barrientos.
Around 300 of Escondida's 1,800 strong workforce are members of the union, he said.
Barrientos said that under Chilean law unions may call for collective pay talks if they represent at least 25 percent of a company's workforce.
The contract will include proposals covering holidays, working conditions and demands for a 10 percent increase in basic wages, he said.
Escondida, which is owned by Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc, has two weeks to reply to the union's demands.
Escondida is the world's largest copper mine and produced over 800,000 tonnes of copper last year.
